gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold concerns the missing grid-weight factor in the local Dirichlet energy and the resulting Poincare/coercivity scaling. ISSUE-001 instead diagnoses a false tensor decomposition and mismatched operator-norm bounds in the fluctuation proof; the shared proposition location does not connect these distinct formula failures.

The gold concerns undefined M_min and M_max extrema on different grids, which makes gamma_h source-undefined. ISSUE-001 contains no diagnosis of missing extrema or undefined constants; it addresses a separate operator decomposition identity.

The gold identifies an extra L_v factor caused by the scalar-mean and weighted-norm estimate, and supplies the normalization needed for the stated gamma_h factor. ISSUE-001 does not address this norm derivation or normalization; its norm bounds concern different velocity operators.

Both entries diagnose the same false tensor decomposition of the discrete Fokker–Planck operator: the stated three-point velocity operators do not expand to the actual stencil, producing incorrect coefficients and invalid accompanying norm estimates. ISSUE-001 explicitly identifies the coefficient mismatch, the required two-point operators, and the resulting failure of the proposition proof.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The claimed tensor-product decomposition and its operator-norm estimates are inconsistent with the actual discrete operator stencil, so the fluctuation-bound proof analyzes the wrong operators.

component_coverage.gold_component: The stated difference operators annihilate velocity-constant vectors and, when grouped into the claimed tensor decomposition, do not reproduce the actual beta-grouped operator; the decomposition identity is therefore false.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-001 directly expands the claimed decomposition, exhibits a coefficient absent from the actual stencil, gives the correct two-point decomposition, and concludes that the algebraic identity is false.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold concerns using a half-grid maximum to bound cell-centered Maxwellian factors and requires a combined maximum. ISSUE-001 does not identify this missing cell-centered bound or the theorem's absorption-condition problem; it concerns a separate stencil decomposition.

The gold concerns the sign in the projected time-update equation and the resulting definition of G. ISSUE-001 contains no diagnosis of the signed update or collision-operator rearrangement; it addresses an unrelated spatial-velocity operator decomposition.
